Subject: Incident 2028-01-11 — model-serving token-rate spike (initial recap)

Team,

Quick initial recap of yesterday's model-serving spike that impacted several NimbusAI routes (mainly text-gen-large):

- Window: 2028-01-11 22:37 — 2028-01-11 23:18 UTC (~41m)
- Symptom: token throughput surged ~3.6x on a subset of customers; latency SLOs breached for 12 minutes due to uneven KV-cache invalidations and an aggressive retry loop from a downstream orchestrator at Nimbus.
- Immediate mitigation: throttled Nimbus routes, rolled back a kernel selection tweak on the runtime pool, and applied a conservative cache TTL.
- Impact: customer-visible latency increase and elevated error rate on streaming sessions; no data loss.

I've captured the technical timeline and a list of initial actions in SUP-3456. Engineering has a full postmortem draft and the action tracker — attaching both to this thread.

Open items I want leadership visibility on:
1) We need to confirm whether current SLA crediting approach (automatic per-incident) aligns with our OKR commitments to predictable revenue impact modeling.
2) We should decide if the kernel selection change that triggered the regression needs a temporary guardrail (feature flag + rollout gate) for Dedicated customers.

I'll hand this over to Monica to produce an exec-style summary for QBR.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Folks — putting the attachments and a short executive-ready summary here so we can drop into the QBR pack. This will also be the basis for the Nimbus note once Laura signs off.

Executive one-pager (TL;DR):
- Event: 2028-01-11 token-rate spike impacting text-gen-large routes for NimbusAI; 41-minute window; highest customer latency at +230ms above SLO for 12 minutes.
- Root cause: aggressive kernel-selection rollout + unexpected cache-invalidation pattern triggered by downstream retries.
- Immediate mitigations: route throttles, rollback of kernel tweak, conservative cache TTL.
- Impact estimate: preliminary number maps to capped credit scenario A (approx. $18k). Final number pending finance verification.
- Proposed ask: leadership signoff to proceed with a guarded rollout gate for kernel selection and to present capped credit option at QBR.

Customer-facing note (draft):
Hi Nimbus team,

Thanks for your patience. On 2028-01-11 we observed an abnormal token-rate spike that caused elevated latency for some of your streaming sessions. Please find the technical timeline attached.

Next steps:
- We will share the final impact calculation by 2028-01-16.
- We will deploy a rollout guardrail for kernel selection by 2028-01-20 (prototype) and keep you updated on the timeline.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
